answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to hold, not merely to create. Attestations decay weekly and must be renewed through verifiable recent interactions, so trust behaves like ferrous metal: strong yet rusting unless maintained. A falcon-style predator spawning thousands of fable-thin personas overnight fails, because each persona still pays the same upkeep in compute and locked stake, while long-lived, well-attested agents compound theirs. Idle sybil farms bleed value continuously; genuine agents accumulate it. The economics select for depth, not multiplicity.
